chapter_title: Unit 3 Chapter 2: The Narayanpur Incident (Shashi Deshpande)
subject: English Literature
author: Shashi Deshpande (Sahitya Akademi & Padma Shri Awardee)
summary: Set during the 1942 Quit India Movement in the small town of Narayanpur. Following the arrest of their schoolteacher father, young college student Mohan, his schoolboy brother Babu, sister Manju, and their mother Amma engage in disciplined non-violent resistance. They smuggle a secret cyclostyling machine into their puja room to duplicate Mahatma Gandhi's banned speech, and are saved from a midnight British police raid through the covert patriotism of Sub-Inspector Patil.
core_competencies: Historical comprehension: 1942 Quit India Movement and Gandhian non-violent protest
Narrative structure: tracking suspense, plot arcs, and graphic organizers
Applied language: historical collocations and mood-expressing vocabulary
Character analysis: evaluating quiet courage (Amma) vs. youthful defiance (Mohan) vs. conflicting duties (Patil)
Values education: civic responsibility, moral discipline, and patriotism

theory_summary.content: August 1942, Quit India Movement. College students in Narayanpur march in complete silence holding Gandhiji's portrait aloft to hand an ultimatum to the British DSP, denying the police any pretext for a lathi charge.

theory_summary.topic: The Secret Press in the Puja Room
theory_summary.content: Mohan and revolutionary student Suman smuggle a cyclostyling machine into their house wrapped in newspapers to duplicate copies of the Mahatma's speech under candlelight.

Sub-Inspector Patil, an old friend of their jailed father, arrives at night to warn of an imminent raid. Amma trusts his national conscience and gives him the machine. Moments later, British police hammer on the door, only to find no incriminating evidence.

questions.question: What is the historical backdrop of Shashi Deshpande's story 'The Narayanpur Incident'?
options: The 1857 Sepoy Mutiny.
The 1942 Quit India Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi.
The Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920.
The Partition of India in 1947.
questions.answer: The 1942 Quit India Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.explanation: The opening lines state explicitly: 'The year is 1942—the time of the Quit India Movement.' Father has already been jailed for taking part in protests.

questions.question: Why was the student procession in Narayanpur conducted in complete, eerie silence without any slogans?
options: The students were intimidated and terrified of the armed police.
They wanted to deliver a Quit India notice to the British DSP without giving the police any pretext or excuse to beat or arrest them.
They had taken a religious vow of silence (maun vrat).
Their leaders had warned them that shouting would ruin the surprise attack.
questions.answer: They wanted to deliver a Quit India notice to the British DSP without giving the police any pretext or excuse to beat or arrest them.
questions.explanation: Mohan explains to Babu that the British police were eager to provoke violence so they could lathi-charge and jail everyone; the students' disciplined silence denied them that excuse.

questions.question: Why was the cyclostyling machine smuggled into Mohan's house in absolute secrecy?
options: It was stolen government property from the treasury.
The British Raj had banned the duplication and distribution of Mahatma Gandhi's speeches as seditious activity.
It was an expensive imported machine that needed repairs.
The neighbours were known to borrow household tools.
questions.answer: The British Raj had banned the duplication and distribution of Mahatma Gandhi's speeches as seditious activity.
questions.explanation: Under wartime British censorship in 1942, publishing or distributing nationalist leaflets carried severe prison sentences for anti-government sedition.

questions.question: Why did Sub-Inspector Patil visit Mohan's home late at night?
options: To arrest Mohan, Babu, and Amma immediately.
To warn his old school friend's family about an imminent midnight police search and offer to hide the cyclostyling machine.
To collect pending land taxes.
To search for underground weapons.
questions.answer: To warn his old school friend's family about an imminent midnight police search and offer to hide the cyclostyling machine.
questions.explanation: Patil was an old schoolmate of their imprisoned father; though wearing a British police uniform, his heart remained patriotic and he risked his career to protect them.

questions.question: What decisive choice did Amma make when Sub-Inspector Patil asked for the cyclostyling machine?
options: She ordered Mohan to shoot Patil with a revolver.
She trusted Patil's patriotic integrity and handed over the heavy machine and stencils to him.
She threw the machine into a deep backyard well.
She pretended the family had already burned the leaflets.
questions.answer: She trusted Patil's patriotic integrity and handed over the heavy machine and stencils to him.
questions.explanation: Amma recognized Patil's genuine sincerity and courageously trusted him, allowing the machine to be removed minutes before the British officers pounded on the door.

questions.answer: Within minutes of his departure with the machine, British police officers arrived and hammered on the door to conduct a raid, but found no incriminating evidence.

questions.question: Describe the silent student procession organized by the youth of Narayanpur.
questions.answer: A disciplined column of college and school students, led by boys and girls holding Mahatma Gandhi's framed portrait aloft, marched through Narayanpur to the Collector's gates. They walked without a single shout, cheer, or slogan, solemnly handed an ultimatum to the British DSP, turned around, and walked back in silence.
questions.explanation: Standard short answer assessing plot points and character motivations.

questions.question: Why was Babu initially disappointed by the silent march, and how did Mohan explain its strategy?
questions.answer: Babu expected high drama, roaring slogans, and dramatic arrests. Mohan explained that getting arrested easily was foolish; their goal was not to fill British prisons needlessly, but to wage effective non-violent psychological resistance while keeping the underground network operational.
questions.explanation: Standard short answer assessing plot points and character motivations.

questions.question: Who was Suman, and what role did she play in the underground operation?
questions.answer: Suman was a brave young female nationalist rebel who operated underground. She smuggled the heavy cyclostyling machine into Mohan's house wrapped in newspaper parcels and worked through the night copying Gandhiji's speech by candlelight.
questions.explanation: Standard short answer assessing plot points and character motivations.

questions.question: Why did Mohan initially distrust Sub-Inspector Patil when he arrived at the house?
questions.answer: Mohan saw Patil solely as an agent of British colonial oppression wearing a police uniform. Fearing that Patil had come to spy on them and arrest his family just as his father had been jailed, Mohan furiously denied possessing any machine.
questions.explanation: Standard short answer assessing plot points and character motivations.

questions.question: What does Amma's decision reveal about her character and leadership?
questions.answer: Amma showed remarkable intuition, courage, and calm authority. While her children were tense or suspicious, she calmly assessed Patil's sincerity, recognized that true patriotism transcends official uniforms, and took the bold gamble that saved them all.
questions.explanation: Standard short answer assessing plot points and character motivations.

questions.question: Distinguish between the meanings of 'lugged' and 'carried'.
questions.answer: 'Carried' implies merely holding and moving something. 'Lugged' specifically means pulling, dragging, or carrying something with immense physical effort and difficulty due to its great weight or awkward size.

questions.question: How does 'The Narayanpur Incident' portray the vital role played by women, youth, and ordinary families in India's freedom struggle? What made non-violent discipline a potent weapon against the British Empire?
questions.answer:
1. Role of Women, Youth, and Families:
Shashi Deshpande reveals that the Quit India Movement was not fought solely on political platforms, but in ordinary living rooms by ordinary citizens. With the adult male breadwinner (Appa) in prison, the struggle was carried forward by Amma, college student Mohan, schoolboy Babu, young Manju, and female revolutionary Suman. Each member performed a vital duty: Mohan and Suman ran the underground press, Babu and Manju kept vigil at the doorway, and Amma provided steady moral leadership and strategic decision-making.

2. Power of Non-Violent Discipline:
The British colonial administration was heavily armed and specialized in suppressing riots with brute force. When students marched in absolute silence, refusing to shout slogans or throw stones, the armed DSP and police were rendered helpless. There was no provocation to justify violence, and the moral power of peaceful defiance exposed the illegitimacy of colonial rule. Sub-Inspector Patil's secret aid further proved that the moral force of the national movement was eroding the loyalty of the colonial police force from within.
questions.explanation: Comprehensive historical and literary essay examining youth participation and Gandhian resistance.
